segments: Verification scope: nixpkgs nixos-unstable modules and upstream documentation consulted in October 2026. Group lists, package counts, and service defaults change across revisions. When deploying, use the nixpkgs and Home Manager source versions locked by your project as the authority. No builds, activations, or desktop runtime tests were performed for this article.
The Complete Startup Chain

Three layers of coordination sit between a bare TTY and a usable desktop. They govern display-device ownership, the user-service environment, and autostart respectively. Troubleshooting requires checking each layer separately.
Layer One: Handing Over DRM Master

In some kmscon configurations using the libseat=false raw-VT backend, the terminal may hold DRM master to render the TTY. This depends on the kmscon version, seat backend, and startup mode. For the compositor to take over the display, kmscon must first release master.
Method: send the terminal the OSC escape \033]setBackground\a → kmscon releases master and moves into the background; after the compositor exits, send setForeground to restore it

kmscon builds supporting this interface may provide kmscon-launch-gui, coordinating the sequence setBackground → 短暂等待 → 运行合成器 → setForeground (setBackground → wait briefly → run the compositor → setForeground). First check whether the tool exists locally and inspect its implementation; do not treat a fixed wait time as a stable protocol.
If DRM master is still held when the compositor starts, startup may fail. A black screen alone does not establish that this is the cause.
Layer Two: uwsm's Session Model
uwsm (Universal Wayland Session Manager) wraps the compositor in a systemd user session:
uwsm start hyprland.desktop → creates units such as wayland-wm@.service and activates graphical-session.target

Some distribution or patched versions may integrate kmscon coordination. The upstream uwsm main source inspected for this article contained no setBackground, so automatic coordination cannot be assumed for every version. Inspect the startup wrapper and seat backend in the version actually locked by your configuration.

graphical-session.target represents part of the systemd user graphical-session lifecycle. uwsm also waits for environment variables and services to be ready; a single active status does not establish that every desktop feature is healthy.
Layer Three: The Two Roles of graphical-session.target
This target serves two roles; understanding them explains much of the seemingly mysterious behavior:
1. Detect whether a compositor is running: uwsm check may-start checks whether the target is active and refuses startup if it is, reporting "compositor already running".

Multiple session managers may leave state behind
If the relevant target remains active after a desktop exits, uwsm's may-start check may reject the next startup. Check the unit relationships, exit logs, and state for the actual version. Do not infer from one failure that a desktop is permanently incompatible with uwsm, and do not blindly stop the target while another session is active.

2. Trigger XDG autostart: systemd's systemd-xdg-autostart-generator creates user services for compatible .desktop files. Actual unit names and conditions depend on the file ID, OnlyShowIn/NotShowIn, the environment, and package versions. uwsm connects the session to xdg-desktop-autostart.target, launching applications whose conditions are met. Other session managers, including GNOME's, also implement autostart; uwsm is not the only way to start fcitx5.

The Cost of Bypassing uwsm Running a compositor directly with only a display-handoff tool may leave the systemd graphical session and autostart target unestablished. If fcitx5 does not start automatically on such a startup path, first check the targets, user services, environment, and desktop-file conditions. Running fcitx5 -d manually is only a diagnostic step, and duplicate instances must be avoided. Input-method failures can also arise from environment variables, protocols, or configuration; they cannot all be reduced to a single cause.
The Correct Procedure for Switching Desktop Environments from a TTY

When the user session can end and be reestablished normally, a system reboot is usually unnecessary. The GNOME example uses GDM + specialisation and is managed by GNOME's session manager; do not additionally wrap its compositor inside another session manager. Driver, kernel, or login-service changes may still require a reboot.
Troubleshooting Quick Reference
Symptom
Check first
A lingering graphical-session.target (check with systemctl --user status)
Compositor fails to start / black screen
DRM/seat permissions, device ownership, display drivers, and compositor logs
fcitx5 does not start automatically
Autostart target, desktop-file conditions, user-service environment, input-method configuration, and duplicate instances
